title: Chrome’s ad-blocking champion gets one last update before the curtain falls
summary: The popular ad blocker has just received its final stable Chrome release.
body: TL;DR uBlock Origin 1.74 is its last stable release for Chrome, with the Chrome Web Store set to remove the extension on August 31. Google has closed the loopholes that kept Manifest V2 extensions running, paving the way for uBlock Origin’s removal from Chrome. You can still block ads in Chrome, but the experience won’t be quite the same as what uBlock Origin offered under Manifest V2. For many Chrome users, uBlock Origin (uBO) has long been one of those essential browser extensions , quietly sitting in the toolbar and blocking ads without much fuss. But Google’s long-running Manifest V2 crackdown has steadily changed that, and the uBlock Origin team has now confirmed that the extension’s run on Chrome will end on August 31. The uBlock Origin team has released version 1.74 , and it comes with a rather significant footnote: this is the last stable uBO version to be available on the Chrome Web Store. The team says the Chrome Web Store will remove uBO on August 31, meaning Chrome users have only days before the extension is officially shown the door. title: The Galaxy S26 Ultra just achieved a first for Android phone sales
summary: Samsung is the sole Android brand in the top 10, but the S26 Ultra also made a notable achievement.
body: Credit: Ryan Haines / Android Authority TL;DR The Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra was the most popular Android phone globally in Q2 2026, according to a new report. This is apparently the first time that an “ultra-premium” phone led Android sales in Q2. The base Galaxy S26 also made the list, along with three Galaxy A phones. The most popular Android phones in a quarter tend to be cheap models. That’s not a surprise, as the lower prices make these phones more accessible than high-end models. However, the latest global market share report reveals a surprising top-seller for Android. Counterpoint Research has posted its Q2 2026 global market share report , and it turns out that the $1,300 Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra was the most popular Android phone in the quarter. Samsung’s Ultra phone was ranked fourth. What’s also interesting is that the base Galaxy S26 landed in ninth place. By contrast, the Galaxy S25 Ultra was in ninth place back in Q2 2025 while the base S25 didn’t feature at all.

title: 5 useless Android apps you probably still download (and why you should stop)

body: Android has come a long way since its inception. Back in the day, doing even the most trivial things, like using the LED next to the rear camera as a flashlight, required third-party flashlight apps . However, that has changed over the years: the operating system has evolved significantly, and it now bundles many advanced features and apps to reduce reliance on third-party apps. That said, many Android users still download third-party apps for various things. Some users do it out of habit — having been installing them on their phones for years. title: The Google Photos redesign broke something I use every day. Here’s how to fix it
summary: Bring back the dates!!
body: If you’ve used Google Photos for years , as I and probably most people reading this have, there are certain features and creature comforts you’ve likely come to rely on. title: This bezel-less phone looks even crazier in its first hands-on video

body: TL;DR TECNO’s 0mm-bezel concept has been shown off in a hands-on video, offering the clearest look yet at the phone ahead of its IFA 2026 showcase. The concept features a 144Hz display, triple rear cameras, a 6,000mAh battery, and a holographic, lenticular back panel TECNO has built a reputation for showcasing unusual smartphone concepts at major tech events. The PHANTOM Ultimate G Fold , billed as the world’s thinnest trifold, debuted ahead of IFA 2025, while MWC 2026 brought an ultra-thin modular phone . Now, a hands-on video of TECNO’s latest concept phone is out, giving us our first proper look at its bezel-less design ahead of its IFA 2026 debut. TECNO itself showcased the 0mm-bezel phone a few weeks ago, teasing its edge-to-edge display without revealing much about what it would be like to actually use. title: Google Photos may soon give you less time to restore deleted media
summary: Google could soon unify trash retention rules and cut the recovery window for backed-up files from 60 days to 30 days.
body: Credit: Taylor Kerns / Android Authority TL;DR Google Photos currently keeps backed-up media in the Trash for 60 days and regular, non-backed-up media for 30 days. Code found in Google Photos v7.90 indicates Google plans to unify this rule, reducing trash retention for all media to 30 days. The change is not yet live, but it will likely be announced with plenty of notice before rolling out broadly. Google appears to be preparing a notable shift in Google Photos, shortening the time deleted photos and videos sit in your trash folder before they vanish forever. While Google has been spotted working on smarter backup solutions, such as overnight backup options , this upcoming change could rationalize how long your discarded media hangs around. title: Camilo’s ‘Vida de Rico’ Enters YouTube’s Billion Views Club
summary: The Colombian singer and songwriter passes one billion streams on YouTube with his feel-good 2020 single “Vida de Rico.”
body: Welcome to the club, Camilo . That is, YouTube’s Billion Views Club. Following its release, “Vida de Rico” climbed to No. 1 on the Latin Airplay chart (dated Jan. 30, 2021), doing so in its 16 th week, and notched multiple weeks atop the Latin Pop Airplay tally. He also performed the number during Billboard ‘s virtual Latin Music Week in 2020, presented during the pandemic, and the following year during the 22nd annual Latin Grammy Awards. title: ألفاريز يفجر مفاجأة جديدة.. وبيان رسمي يكشف الحقيقة
summary: النجم الأرجنتيني يزيد الجدل حول مستقبله
body: النجم الأرجنتيني يزيد الجدل حول مستقبله غاب الأرجنتيني جوليان ألفاريز مهاجم أتلتيكو مدريد، عن تدريبات فريقه اليوم الأربعاء، بعد يومين من الراحة التي حصل عليها لاعبو الروخيبلانكوس. وبدأ أتلتيكو مدريد مشوار الليجا يوم السبت الماضي بالتعادل (2-2) أمام فياريال، على ملعب متروبوليتانو. وذكر بيان رسمي صادر من نادي أتلتيكو مدريد، نشرته صحيفة " ماركا " الإسبانية، أن ألفاريز غاب عن التدريبات بسبب المرض. وشارك ألفاريز كبديل في الدقيقة 66 من مباراة أتلتيكو مدريد وفياريال، وقوبل بصيحات استهجان من قبل جماهير ناديه. وأضافت الصحيفة أن غياب ألفاريز يزيد من حدة الجدل حول مستقبله ، والذي سيتم تحديده في الأول من سبتمبر/أيلول المقبل، بمجرد إغلاق سوق الانتقالات، ومعرفة أين سيلعب هذا الموسم. وكان ألفاريز قد أعلن رغبته في ترك أتلتيكو مدريد، أثناء مشاركته مع منتخب الأرجنتين في كأس العالم 2026، ما أثار حفيظة النادي المدريدي. ويعتبر برشلونة الهدف الأول للمهاجم الأرجنتيني في ظل رغبة كبيرة من النادي الكتالوني في التعاقد معه، لكن على الجانب الآخر لا يزال أتلتيكو مدريد متمسك بخدماته ويرفض بيعه للبلوجرانا. ويستعد أتلتيكو مدريد حاليًا لخوض مواجهته الثانية في الليجا أمام إشبيلية يوم السبت المقبل. يمكنكم مناقشة الموضوعات والأخبار بشكل أعمق في منتديات كووورة

title: Lenovo’s first Android handheld lets you stream PC games without a network connection
summary: No network for game streaming? No problem.
body: Credit: Lenovo TL;DR Lenovo has launched the Legion Cloud Gaming Handheld C700 in China. The handheld has a dongle that allows you to stream games from a PC without a network connection. Expect to pay ~$327 for this Android handheld. The Android handheld space has become highly competitive, as companies like ANBERNIC, Retroid, and AYANEO all duke it out with interesting products. Now, Lenovo has decided to step into the arena with a newly launched Android handheld of its own. Lenovo launched the Legion Cloud Gaming Handheld C700 in China this week, coming months after we first heard about it . This is a huge Android handheld designed for (surprise) cloud gaming. The device supports “one-touch” streaming from a PC via Lenovo’s proprietary Legion Stream protocol and an included dongle. In fact, the company says you can stream games while offline. That could be handy if you’re traveling.

summary: أسطورة برشلونة يجيد الألعاب النفسية مع الصحافة

title: Perplexity launches a local AI agent with zero token costs
summary: All you need is a $5,000 NVIDIA setup.
body: TL;DR Perplexity has launched a new agentic AI tool called “Portable Computer” that runs locally on users’ devices. It uses small, efficient models such as Qwen 3.8 and NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning. It will not incur token costs for tasks completed locally, but can connect to cloud models if needed. Months after launching its agentic AI tool, “Personal Computer,” Perplexity is introducing a new option for users who prefer to run their AI agents locally . The company today announced “Portable Computer,” its local-first agent, in partnership with NVIDIA. Portable Computer will run entirely on-device. The agent, along with the models and other tools, lives locally on the user’s device. This ensures that user data isn’t sent to the cloud and offers a higher level of privacy for sensitive data.

title: رسميًا.. الأهلي يحسم مصير إمام عاشور
summary: نهاية الجدل
body: نهاية الجدل حسم الأهلي المصري رسميًا، مصير لاعبه إمام عاشور، في ظل الجدل الدائر حول مستقبله خلال الفترة الماضية، وتحديدًا بعد نهاية مونديال 2026. وتزايدت الأنباء حول احتمالية رحيل إمام عاشور عن القلعة الحمراء في الصيف الحالي، وسط اهتمام من أندية تركية وسعودية. لكن الأهلي حسم الجدل في ملف إمام عاشور، وأعلن تجديد عقده رسميًا، ليستمر ضمن صفوف الفريق الأحمر حتى عام 2030. يمكنكم مناقشة الموضوعات والأخبار بشكل أعمق في منتديات كووورة وقال الأهلي في بيان رسمي نشره في الساعات الأولى من صباح اليوم الأربعاء: "قام إمام عاشور، لاعب الفريق الأول لكرة القدم، بتمديد تعاقده مع النادي حتى عام 2030. جاء ذلك خلال جلسة جمعته مع الدكتور عصام سراج الدين، رئيس قطاع التعاقدات، الذي أنهى كافة الإجراءات الإدارية والمالية بالتنسيق الكامل مع الكابتن وائل جمعة، مدير الكرة". وأضاف البيان: "خلال الجلسة أكد اللاعب، على امتنانه الكامل للأهلي وجماهيره الكبيرة ورغبته في استكمال مسيرته مع النادي خلال السنوات القادمة". ويستعد الأهلي لخوض مباراته الثانية في الدوري المصري الممتاز، مساء الجمعة المقبل ضد زد، علمًا بأن إمام عاشور غاب عن المباراة الأولى التي انتصر فيها الفريق الأحمر ضد الشرقية إنبي (3-2) . 🔴 إمام عاشور يمدد تعاقده مع النادي حتى عام 2030 🦅 pic.twitter.com/dRlKkNO9us — ‏النادي الأهلي (@AlAhly) August 25, 20…

title: Savage Garden’s Darren Hayes’ Career Celebrated at Music In The House Gala
summary: The Australian singer and songwriter received two awards on the night.
body: It was anything but an ordinary Tuesday night (Aug. 27) in Sydney as Darren Hayes was feted with the Excellence in Community Award at the 17th annual Music In The House event. The ex- Savage Garden singer and songwriter was on hand at the Support Act fundraiser, presented at The Linseed House, The Grounds of Alexandria, where he doubled up with induction into APRA AMCOS’s Billions Club — recognition of the pop group’s Billboard Hot 100 leader from 1997, “Truly Madly Deeply,” one of their two U.S. No. 1s. Savage Garden, the pairing of Hayes and Daniel Jones, was one of Australia’s biggest exports of the 1990s. Their self-titled debut album — which houses “Truly Madly Deeply” and top 10 hit “I Want You” — peaked at No. 3 on the Billboard 200, while sophomore and final release Affirmation , which houses No. 1 smash “I Knew I Loved You,” reached No. 6. title: Fan survey sends Google a pretty blunt message about the Pixel 12

body: Like it or not, Google has made AI a huge part of the Pixel experience, and that’s only become more obvious with the Pixel 11 series. It’s always quite tricky to know how true that is, so we were curious about where you think Google needs to go next with the Pixel 12. We recently asked our readers exactly that. My colleague Robert Trigg certainly has his own ideas about this direction, and made them abundantly clear in a recent article . His argument in a nutshell is that the Pixel 11 shows Google is approaching something of a hardware breaking point. He wasn’t unhappy with Google’s AI work, but pointed out that rival flagships are pushing ahead in fundamental areas such as battery capacity, charging speeds, camera hardware, and raw performance, while Pixels haven’t kept pace. With the Pixel 12 next to face that challenge, we asked you via a poll in the article whether Google should prioritize better hardware, even smarter AI, both, or simply more competitive prices.

body: TL;DR Some Google Home users are facing a bug where the voice assistant refuses to add items to their Google Keep lists. While not all users appear to be facing this issue, it appears widespread enough for Google to take notice. Meanwhile, a quick look at Google Home settings suggests that access to notes & lists using a voice assistant may have been removed. It feels like we’re reporting on a Google Home bug or a fix almost every other day. Only today, users received some good news following reports of devices refusing to set alarms over voice commands. Sadly, those good times aren’t going to last, and it now looks like yet another function is being impacted by a similar glitch, as some people are seemingly unable to add items to their lists on Google Keep using Google Home voice commands. In a series of complaints on Reddit, including one from Friday, a user claims the voice assistant recognizes their commands perfectly well, but refuses to add items to the list . For instance, if the person asks one of their Google Home devices to “add x to list xyz,” the assistant might respond by saying how many items are on that list, while refusing to add any new items.

title: Google Home made users say the weirdest thing to set an alarm, but that’s over now
summary: It's a small fix, but a welcome one for anyone who relies on voice alarms daily.
body: TL;DR Some Google Home devices stopped setting alarms via voice command for several days. The bug hit both Google Assistant and Gemini for Home, affecting Nest speakers, displays, and even third-party devices like Lenovo smart displays. Google has confirmed the fix, and our own testing shows alarms are setting and triggering correctly again. Google Home has had a busy August, with Google rolling out several updates that make Gemini for Home smarter and add new capabilities to its smart home platform. But amid all those improvements, something as basic as setting an alarm suddenly stopped working for some users. Thankfully, Google has now confirmed that the issue affecting Nest and other Gemini-powered smart home devices has been fixed. For several days, users on Reddit reported that commands such as “Hey Google, set an alarm for 8:30 AM” would simply be ignored. Some found that alarms worked when set for an exact hour, while others had to ask Google to set an alarm first and then provide the time when prompted. One odd workaround involved saying “Hey Google, hi” before giving the alarm command.

title: The Pixel 11 Pro’s camera flash is a ‘LoLight’ thanks to HiLight
summary: Users complain that the Pixel 11 Pro's camera flash is a big downgrade over other phones, and HiLight could be to blame here.
body: Credit: Sanuj Bhatia / Android Authority TL;DR Reddit users report that the Google Pixel 11 Pro’s camera flash is significantly weaker than that of older Pixels and competitors. Our preliminary testing here at Android Authority shows the Pixel 11 Pro XL torch mode registered 89 lux compared to 123 lux on the Pixel 10 Pro XL. The physical diffuser added to the camera visor for the new HiLight LED array is likely the cause of the softer beam. Google’s new Pixel 11 Pro series introduces HiLight , a small array of ambient LEDs around the camera flash that give you some bits of information without requiring you to turn over or unlock your phone. Google ended up severely limiting HiLight’s functionality, and users had to resort to apps like HiLight Studio to unlock the LED’s full potential. As it turns out, Google gimped HiLight in more ways than one, with the LED flash itself also downgraded compared to the Pixel 10 series. Reddit user pcman2000 voiced their frustration with the Pixel 11 Pro’s camera flash, calling it “really weak” and the weakest among all the phones they tested, ranking it below the Pixel 9 Pro and even the iPhone 17e.

title: The Galaxy Z Fold 8 has a camera problem, and it has nothing to do with photo quality

body: I’ve spent years trying the latest book-style foldables, but none earned a permanent spot in my pocket once I finished testing them. Unfortunately, it suffered from the same problems as every other folding phone with a squarish inner screen aspect ratio. The form factor isn’t conducive to widescreen video content, as you’ll see large black bars at the top and bottom of the folding screen. Samsung built the wide Galaxy Z Fold 8 to specifically address this pain point, and it quickly won me over. Then, something happened that I didn’t expect. I found myself using the Galaxy Z Fold 8 unfolded in portrait orientation more than landscape.

It can diagnose battery and Wi-Fi issues, open specific settings, change things like brightness and dark mode, and explain Pixel features without making you hunt through Settings. It’s still a Labs feature and can get things wrong. Our testing produced inconsistent instructions for Magic Capture, so it isn’t completely reliable yet. A few days ago, we spotted Google testing a clever new Gemini trick that could save Pixel users from digging through the Settings app every time something goes wrong. That feature, called Device Help, is now appearing directly inside the Gemini app on some of our Pixel 11 series devices. First spotted by 9to5Google , Device Help is currently showing up on Pixel 11 and Pixel 11 Pro models we’ve checked, including our Pixel 11 Pro XL units. It still has a “Labs” badge attached, though, which is Google’s way of telling you things may not always work as expected. And after putting it through a few tests, that’s exactly what we found.

title: Google’s Tensor G7 has one last chance to save the Pixel 12

body: The Pixel 11 series has left Google with something of a dilemma. Based on our time with the phones so far, they remain among the most enjoyable Android handsets to use, thanks largely to Google’s software experience and a growing collection of genuinely useful features. But our testing of the Tensor G6 shows that Google’s custom silicon is falling further behind rival flagship chips; early gaming tests suggest a familiar litany of issues; and a week with the Pixel 11 Pro suggests that many of Google’s newest AI tricks aren’t yet strong enough to make up the difference. body: Credit: Kaitlyn Cimino / Android Authority TL;DR An unofficial project brings Quick Share receiving to jailbroken Kindle devices. Kindshare lets you send files wirelessly from an Android phone, but the Kindle can’t send files back. The process is fairly technical, and compatibility may depend on your Kindle model and firmware version. Quick Share made an unexpected leap beyond Android last year when Google made it compatible with Apple’s AirDrop . Now it’s more or less reached another device you probably wouldn’t have expected, as an unofficial project lets you send files from an Android phone straight to a jailbroken Kindle. As spotted by Hackaday , developer unrealJune has created Kindshare, an open-source project that adds Quick Share receiving to compatible Kindles. Once everything is set up, the Kindle can appear as a destination in Quick Share, letting you send files over wirelessly.

title: Spotify bug leaves Android Auto drivers staring at error message
summary: Spotify not working for you on Android Auto? You're not alone.
body: Credit: Andy Walker / Android Authority TL;DR Android Auto users are reporting issues with Spotify. The app is displaying an error message that reads “Spotify isn’t responding.” It’s unclear what the cause of the problem is. Sometimes being an Android Auto user can feel like playing a game of whack-a-mole. A bug appears, a fix is rolled out, and another bug appears shortly after. For example, a fix for a glitch that caused connections to drop or freeze was recently released . Now, a new bug has shown up, and it’s preventing users from streaming their music and podcasts. According to several Android Auto users on Reddit ( 1 , 2 ), the latest issue affects the Spotify app. When attempting to access the app, these users are running into an error message that reads “Spotify isn’t responding.” The screen includes options to exit the app or to wait for it to start working again.

title: The Pixel 11 Pro XL is built to last and easy to fix, teardown finds
summary: It's pricey, but at least you'll be able to hold onto it a few years.
body: TL;DR JerryRigEverything’s Zack Nelson has tested the Pixel 11 Pro XL’s durability and repairability. The phone didn’t bend in Nelson’s durability test, and key components are relatively simple to swap out. Nelson calls the Pixel 11 Pro XL “one of the easiest phones to repair of 2026.” It looks like it should be relatively easy to make the Pixel 11 Pro last. The XL version has now undergone the JerryRigEverything treatment, and the phone held up nicely to Zack Nelson’s usual battery of abuse. The teardown video also shows that common repairs should be relatively simple, with both the display and the battery removable with just a few minutes of work. The video shows that the 11 Pro XL barely bends or flexes at all as Nelson wrenches on it, so the phone should hold up fine in case you sit down with it in your back pocket. Despite Google’s claim that the 11 Pro’s display is “more than twice as scratch-resistant than previous models” thanks to a new coating, though, it still scratches at level six with deeper grooves at a level seven.

title: Netflix is reportedly in talks to add rival streamers like Peacock
summary: Netflix could soon open up its service to other streamers.
body: Credit: Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority TL;DR Netflix could soon let you access other rival streamers through its platform. The company is reportedly in talks with Peacock and Fox One. It’s unclear if Netflix would sell subscriptions to those streamers or just include their content directly in the app. From Peacock to ESPN , there’s been a rash of streaming-related price hikes lately. If you’re worried that this article will be about Netflix announcing a rate increase, you can rest easy. That’s not happening, at least not yet anyway. Rather, this has to do with Netflix reportedly opening up its service to its rivals. It appears that Netflix is interested in becoming a one-stop shop for streaming. The New York Times reports that Netflix is considering adding shows and movies from other streaming services. The company is said to be currently in talks with Peacock and Fox One to bring their content to the platform.

title: The Galaxy S27 Ultra may debut with self-healing glass
summary: Android Authority remembers the LG G Flex 2.
body: TL;DR A rumor claims glass used in the Samsung Galaxy S27 Ultra could come with a self-healing layer that fills in minor scratches on its own. The glass is purportedly being developed jointly by Corning and Samsung. The Samsung Galaxy S27 Ultra may introduce an interesting feature that sounds like it could be a real benefit to users. A rumor from this weekend claims that Samsung’s upcoming Ultra flagship will come with self-healing glass that’s able to recover from minor scratches on its own. Late last week, industry observer Schrödinger took to X to say that Corning and Samsung are jointly working on “ a new self-healing surface coating” for the next iteration of the former’s Gorilla Armor glass. This coating would certainly be less scratch-resistant than conventional tempered glass, but if it’s able to fill in hairline scratches on its own, that trade-off could be worth it.

title: ESPN’s streaming plans are getting more expensive: Here’s what you’ll pay
summary: Bundles including Disney Plus and Hulu are also affected.
body: TL;DR ESPN streaming plans and bundles are increasing in price. Plans are increasing by $1 to $3 per month. Adjustments also affect many streaming bundles that include ESPN. Last week, we learned that Verizon will soon increase the prices for its Disney Plus, ESPN, and Hulu perks , with plan add-ons increasing by a buck or two per month starting in September. Now, ESPN has announced that its streaming subscriptions and the bundles they’re included in will be going up in price for everyone, not just Verizon subscribers. As we’ve learned from 9to5Mac , ESPN has announced price hikes for its ESPN Select and ESPN Unlimited streaming plans. Select is increasing from $13 to $14 per month (or $140 per year, up from $130), while Unlimited is jumping from $30 to $32 per month (or $320 per year, from $300). Bundles including ESPN along with Disney Plus and Hulu are going up, too.

title: Microsoft will pay you to get your friends using Edge
summary: Get 500 points for every successful referral.
body: TL;DR Microsoft is rolling out a referral program that gives Edge users 500 Microsoft Rewards points for every successful referral. You can earn up to 7,500 points per month, worth roughly $6.82 toward Microsoft or Xbox gift cards. Referrals only count when a new Edge Mobile user installs through your link and searches with Edge on two different days within 14 days. Microsoft really wants you to try out its Edge browser — and it’s willing to put its money where its mouth is. The tech giant has previously awarded Edge usage over competing browsers with monetary incentives, and it is now paying users for convincing others to make the switch.

title: YouTube is bringing lots more content types to 24/7 Stations feeds
summary: Tuning you in to some new ideas for Stations.
body: TL;DR YouTube introduced Stations earlier this year, featuring 24/7 content streams from musical artists. Now Google is expanding Stations to also include podcasts, creator content, and more. Access is only getting started with a small number of creators initially. Like any good streaming service, YouTube is always working to find the next big hook that will keep viewers glued to their screens, video after video. Earlier this year, we spotted a fresh addition to YouTube’s offerings in the form of Stations , 24/7 streams that appeared designed to connect you with an endless feed of content from your favorite musical artists. And now, Stations are getting a bit of an expansion. YouTube is constantly trying out new experiments, and this month, the service shares that its latest involves building Stations around even more diverse content than just music. While you’ll still see Stations from musical performers, they’re also starting to expand to cover podcasts, media channels, and just regular creator content.

title: YouTube fixes the bug that made your comments and video details vanish
summary: The latest update restores the interface that vanished when you exited full screen.
body: TL;DR Google has confirmed that YouTube’s full-screen bug that made video details and comments disappear has been fixed. The fix is rolling out with the latest YouTube update, which affected users can now download. The update should also eliminate the need for the portrait-to-landscape workaround used to restore the missing interface. YouTube’s latest updates are giving its video player another small UI makeover , but there’s more happening than just changing more how you scrub through videos. According to Google support, we’re also getting a fix for an annoying iPad bug that was making comments, titles, descriptions, and other video details disappear after exiting full screen. As we had previously reported , the issue left a blank void beneath the video player whenever affected users returned from full-screen playback. The missing interface elements wouldn’t come back even after switching videos, restarting the iPad, or reinstalling the app.

title: Philips Hue is working on a more affordable TV sync box
summary: It's apparently a lot less expensive, but it won't do as much.
body: TL;DR A UK retailer has listed the unannounced Philips Hue Play Sync Box Lite. The new version offers only a single HDMI input, among other compromises. It’s cool, but it’s also wildly expensive at an MSRP of $385. Now, though, it looks like Philips Hue is set to release a new, stripped-back version at a more affordable price. title: YouTube’s latest UI change improves how you get to a video’s juicy bits
summary: The update adds a visual timeline indicator when double-tapping to skip.
body: TL;DR YouTube may be rolling out a new seek UI on Android that shows how much time you’ve skipped through a video. The change appears on the stable YouTube app, but it hasn’t reached every device. The new behavior could be part of a broader YouTube UI refresh. YouTube’s interface has become something of a moving target lately. The company was only recently testing a new button arrangement on Android that removed text labels from the controls under videos. And now, a small change to how YouTube shows skipped time appears to be rolling out to some Android users. The change involves YouTube’s familiar double-tap gesture for skipping. Currently, you can double-tap the right side of the screen to jump forward or the left side to rewind, while touching and holding the scrub bar lets you manually move through the video. In the current UI, double-tapping skips forward or backward without showing how much time you’ve moved. When manually scrubbing, however, YouTube displays the amount of time you’ve skipped in the video interface, as seen in the screenshot below.

title: Now Playing on Pixel may be getting its big missing feature back
summary: Google could bring back Now Playing notifications after breaking them with a recent update.
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR Google updated the Now Playing app on Pixel earlier this year — and removed the option to show notifications. It may now be working to bring notifications back. Google also appears to be working to add support for multiple users, which isn’t supported yet. Now Playing remains one of the most compelling reasons to buy a Pixel still . In March this year, Google brought a major update to Now Playing, advancing it with its own dedicated app . But the update also brought a few feature cutbacks and challenges, such as removing notifications about tracks being played in your surroundings. This broke popular use cases for using Now Playing’s notifications to import songs into apps, such as Last.fm. What followed was dissatisfaction from users, which Google is now looking to address. It is working to add notifications for the currently playing track back to the app with a future update.

title: Chrome’s new rules ruined ad blockers. Here are 4 things that still work
summary: You can still block ads — just not how you used to.
body: Credit: Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority A few years ago, Chrome introduced Manifest V3 and began phasing out the older Manifest V2 technology used by some of the most advanced browser extensions. According to Google, the older version was harder to maintain and had its own real security risks, but we suspect it’s also because Google wanted to rein in extension capabilities. Unfortunately, this also made it harder to install extensions like the highly popular uBlock Origin. While workarounds still existed by using Chrome flags, that’s no longer the case . It is now virtually impossible to get MV2 extensions to work in Chrome.

title: Galaxy S26 Ultra’s portrait lighting trick could be coming to the S25 Ultra
summary: The feature could help brighten subjects in uneven lighting.
body: TL;DR A leaked One UI 9 build shows the Galaxy S25 Ultra testing a tool that brightens backlit subjects without blowing out the background. The feature, Virtual Reflector, debuted on the Galaxy S26 Ultra and simulates a physical photography reflector in software. Samsung hasn’t confirmed a One UI 9 beta for the S25 series yet, so the feature could still be changed or dropped before release. Samsung appears to be preparing more than a routine software update for the Galaxy S25 series. Recent One UI 9 internal builds have already revealed camera features such as Horizontal Lock and My FanCam , and now another Galaxy S26 Ultra feature has surfaced on the Galaxy S25 Ultra. This time, Samsung could be giving its 2025 flagship a useful new tool to help with portraits in tricky lighting. Leaker Fahad Ali Javed shared screenshots on X showing the Virtual Reflector tool running on a Galaxy S25 Ultra with an internal One UI 9 build ending in ZZHC. SamMobile has also reported on the discovery, noting that Samsung is testing the feature through its Expert RAW camera app.

title: Google, take note: This phone maker’s new chipset looks like an absolute beast
summary: It even has an unannounced GPU.
body: TL;DR Xiaomi has announced the XRing 03 smartphone chipset. This chipset has an unannounced Arm G2-Ultra NX GPU and a 10-core CPU with no little cores. The chip will debut in the Xiaomi 18 Fold, which is scheduled to launch next month. Google has just launched the Pixel 11 series , and our own benchmarks show that the Tensor G6 chip is a significant step down from rival chips. Now, Xiaomi has revealed its XRing 03 processor, and it seemingly obliterates Google’s silicon on paper. Xiaomi revealed XRing 03 details on Weibo , and it packs a 3nm design from an unspecified foundry. However, what’s particularly interesting is that it comes with an unannounced Arm G2-Ultra NX GPU. Expect 16 cores, eight NX neural accelerators, and AI-based super-resolution/frame interpolation. In fact, Xiaomi claims that this GPU is 85% faster than last year’s XRing 01 , 64% more efficient, and 182% faster at ray tracing. For what it’s worth, the XRing 01 had an Immortalis G925 MC16 GPU. Either way, this seems far more impressive than the Tensor G6’s PowerVR CXTP-48-1536 GPU.

title: I want to love the Pixel 11 Pro Fold, but one silly change is stopping me
summary: To make the Pixel 11 Pro Fold roughly 1mm thinner, Google made this compromise.
body: Before the Pixel 11 Pro Fold became official, I shared a wishlist of changes I wanted Google to make for its next foldable. To my surprise, the Pixel 11 Pro Fold offers many of the upgrades I needed to take Google foldables seriously again. It’s thinner and lighter, has slimmer bezels and better screens, and supports faster 25W Qi2 wireless charging. However, Google also made an unexpected change to the Pixel 11 Pro Fold that I can’t overlook. To make the Pixel 11 Pro Fold about 1mm thinner than the Pixel 10 Pro Fold, compromises had to be made. The one you probably noticed is the smaller 4,806mAh battery capacity, but that isn’t the one I care about.
